Keep your records
in one clear place.

Inventory and internal tools that help your team see what is available, what has changed and what needs attention.

Discuss a system
Clarity.

Getting a clear answer should not mean checking five places.

When records are spread across messages, notebooks and spreadsheets, it is hard to know which version to trust. We work through the information your team needs and how it should be updated.

We can build a focused system or help configure existing software when it fits. The right starting point might be stock movements, job tracking or another routine your team needs to manage.

What we can
build together.

The scope is shaped around your requirements. Here is what that can involve.

Requirements grounded in your work

Understand the records, roles, decisions and reporting needs that the system must support.

A focused first version

Agree the essential workflows and build a usable scope rather than an oversized feature list.

Testing and a support plan

Check realistic records and edge cases, then agree training, deployment and maintenance needs.

A clear scope.
Before a commitment.

We start by understanding your business, the tools you use and the outcome you need. Then we agree on deliverables, responsibilities, integrations, costs and checkpoints.

Hosting, provider subscriptions, messaging accounts and ongoing support are discussed where they apply. No hidden assumption that everything is included.

Talk through your requirements

A few useful
answers.

Do you already have an inventory product?+

Our inventory-management project is still in development. We can discuss a custom system around your workflow, with the backend, access and operating requirements agreed before a live deployment.

Can the system connect to our other tools?+

We assess available integrations and agree the data flows and access requirements during planning.

How do you decide what to build first?+

We prioritise the workflow that solves the most useful problem, then agree a focused scope and checkpoints.
